text:
The New York Times caught up with Samuel Girard this month under the headline "Three years sober, the Penguins' Sam Girard has 'become me again'," and on the ice it shows. Nine points in 19 games is a better pace than the 19 he managed in 60 games with Colorado last season, and Pittsburgh gives him 19 minutes a night to move the puck.

Some of the scoring is shooting luck. Three goals on 26 shots is 11.5%, well above the 5% to 9% range we'd expect for him. But the bigger luck story runs the other way: Pittsburgh has scored 9.7 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 5.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 86th percentile among defensemen, which is the earliest sign of assists to come. The one caution comes from Evolving-Hockey: he spent last season beside very strong teammates in Colorado, which flattered his raw numbers. On a Penguins team that has won two of its last ten, there is less help now.
